content.user_title: Build Molecular ML Workflows with DeepChem
content.value_statement: Molecular machine learning often requires specialized featurizers, datasets, and evaluation methods. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code design DeepChem workflows for property prediction, transfer learning, and benchmarks.
actual_capabilities: Select DeepChem featurizers for SMILES strings, molecular graphs, descriptors, and pretrained models.
Guide MoleculeNet benchmark workflows for classification, regression, and materials datasets.
Draft training flows for graph neural networks such as GCN, GAT, MPNN, and AttentiveFP.
Support transfer learning plans with ChemBERTa, GROVER, and MolFormer style models.
Explain evaluation choices for solubility, toxicity, binding affinity, and ADMET prediction.
Use included scripts for solubility prediction, graph neural network training, and transfer learning examples.
limitations: Requires DeepChem and compatible scientific Python dependencies to run examples.
Model quality depends on dataset size, label quality, and molecular split strategy.
Large graph neural network training may need GPU resources and memory tuning.
The skill provides workflow guidance, not validated scientific conclusions.

use_cases.title: Prioritize drug candidates
use_cases.description: Estimate solubility, toxicity, or activity trends before costly laboratory screening.

use_cases.title: Prototype molecular models
use_cases.description: Compare fingerprints, descriptors, and graph neural networks on a custom molecular dataset.

use_cases.title: Teach chemistry ML workflows
use_cases.description: Create guided examples that explain featurization, scaffold splitting, metrics, and benchmark evaluation.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a featurizer
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose a DeepChem featurizer for a CSV file with SMILES strings and one solubility target. Explain the tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Train a benchmark model
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a DeepChem workflow to train a graph convolution model on Tox21 with scaffold splitting and ROC-AUC evaluation.

prompt_templates.title: Use transfer learning
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a transfer learning workflow for a small binding affinity dataset using a pretrained molecular model and proper validation.

prompt_templates.title: Compare model strategies
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare CircularFingerprint, RDKitDescriptors, GCN, and AttentiveFP for my ADMET dataset. Recommend an experiment plan and metrics.

output_examples.input: I have 800 molecules with SMILES and solubility labels. What should I try first?
output: Start with CircularFingerprint and a simple regression model as a baseline.
Use ScaffoldSplitter to reduce chemical leakage between train and test sets.
Consider transfer learning if the baseline is unstable or the labels are sparse.

output_examples.input: I need to evaluate toxicity prediction on Tox21.
output: Use a MoleculeNet Tox21 loader with graph features and scaffold splitting.
Train a multitask classifier because Tox21 has multiple toxicity tasks.
Report ROC-AUC per task and include missing-label handling in the evaluation notes.

output_examples.input: My graph model is running out of memory.
output: Reduce batch size before changing the model architecture.
Use disk-backed datasets for large feature arrays.
Start with a fingerprint baseline to confirm the dataset and labels are usable.

best_practices: Use scaffold splitting for molecular prediction tasks to reduce structure-based data leakage.
Start with simple fingerprint baselines before training deep graph neural networks.
Match metrics to the task type, such as ROC-AUC for classification and RMSE or R2 for regression.
anti_patterns: Do not use random splits for drug discovery claims when similar scaffolds may appear in both sets.
Do not train large graph neural networks on very small datasets without strong regularization or transfer learning.
Do not treat predicted molecular properties as experimental evidence without external validation.

faq.question: What is this skill best for?
faq.answer: It is best for planning and explaining DeepChem workflows for molecular property prediction, benchmarks, and transfer learning.

faq.question: Can it run DeepChem models directly?
faq.answer: It can guide code and scripts, but execution requires a local environment with DeepChem and its dependencies installed.

faq.question: Which featurizer should I start with?
faq.answer: Start with CircularFingerprint for a fast baseline, then try graph featurizers when you have enough data.

faq.question: Why is scaffold splitting recommended?
faq.answer: Scaffold splitting keeps related molecular structures together and gives a more realistic estimate of generalization.

faq.question: Does it support pretrained models?
faq.answer: Yes. The documentation covers transfer learning patterns for models such as ChemBERTa, GROVER, and MolFormer.

faq.question: Is this a substitute for laboratory validation?
faq.answer: No. The skill helps build computational workflows, but results should be validated with appropriate scientific methods.
